comment: The CSS -> SVG contract of the data-visualization widgets, the third category outside the component tier and the mirror image of runtime-contract.json. A chart is drawn in SVG from JS, so the theme publishes what those widgets paint with and the chart themes in packages/devextreme/js/__internal/viz write the reference itself into the markup: `fill: var(--dx-viz-bg, #ffffff)`. Nothing is read back from the document while painting, which is why a chart repaints the moment one of these names changes, and why a chart inside a mode scope paints in that scope's mode. Only what is handed to the application - getColor(), the public palette and theme functions, an export - is read back, at the moment it is asked for. The literal beside each reference is the fallback for a page that loaded another theme; it is the value the name itself carries, and tests/viz-contract.test.ts holds it to the built bundle so the two cannot drift. tests/fluent-next-naming.test.ts excludes the names from the public-surface checks because the reader is not this package.

variables.name: --dx-viz-bg
variables.paints: the surface every widget draws on: chart background, loading panel, export menu, map background, candlestick body, sparkline point, the gap between funnel sections

variables.name: --dx-viz-bg-hovered
variables.paints: the export menu button under the pointer, and the shelf behind a tree map group

variables.name: --dx-viz-bg-higher
variables.paints: the shelf a bar gauge draws its bars on: a plate lifted off the surface, far enough from it to read in a light page

variables.name: --dx-viz-bg-active
variables.paints: the export menu button while pressed or focused

variables.name: --dx-viz-content
variables.paints: text at full strength - titles, export menu, map labels - and the marks that have to stand out against the surface: constant lines, error bars, map selection borders, range selector ticks and the bullet target

variables.name: --dx-viz-content-orange
variables.paints: a map line that is selected: the strongest step of the orange the line family is drawn in

variables.name: --dx-viz-content-subtle
variables.paints: the quieter text and the axis: the widget font colour that axis and legend labels take, the axis line and its ticks, the subtitle under the chart title, tree map group labels, the map control bar border

variables.name: --dx-viz-border
variables.paints: lines that frame something: pane and label borders, annotation border, gauge range container, axis breaks, map background border

variables.name: --dx-viz-border-hovered
variables.paints: the export menu button outline under the pointer

variables.name: --dx-viz-border-active
variables.paints: the export menu button outline while pressed or focused

variables.name: --dx-viz-gray-subtle
variables.paints: the quieter half of a pair that carries no meaning of its own: a losing bar of a win-loss sparkline, a bar below zero, the gauge needle the theme falls back to, and the fill of a map area

variables.name: --dx-viz-indigo-subtle
variables.paints: the triangle marker a gauge puts on its scale for a subvalue

variables.name: --dx-viz-orange-subtle
variables.paints: a map line at rest

variables.name: --dx-viz-red-subtle
variables.paints: the second half of a two-colour gauge needle

variables.name: --dx-viz-grid
variables.paints: the grid: major and minor grid lines, legend border, tree map group border

variables.name: --dx-viz-tile-border
variables.paints: the hairline that separates two tree map tiles. It is drawn on top of the tiles, not on the surface, so it does not follow the mode: the tile under it is a palette colour in both

variables.name: --dx-viz-blue
variables.paints: the first series colour, the near end of the gradient set the tree map and the map mix their scales from, and the shapes that are data rather than chrome: bullet bar, gauge range bar, sparkline line, map markers and the map legend marker

variables.name: --dx-viz-gray
variables.paints: a data shape the design deliberately leaves without meaning: a winning bar of a win-loss sparkline, a bar above zero, and the link between two sankey nodes, grey rather than green on purpose

variables.name: --dx-viz-red
variables.paints: the second series colour, the falling half of an indicating set, the falling bar of a candlestick or a stock series, and the highest point of a sparkline

variables.name: --dx-viz-green
variables.paints: the third series colour, the rising half of an indicating set, and the far end of the gradient set

variables.name: --dx-viz-yellow
variables.paints: the fourth series colour, the middle of an indicating set, and the lowest point of a sparkline

variables.name: --dx-viz-orange
variables.paints: a map line under the pointer

variables.name: --dx-viz-pink
variables.paints: the fifth series colour

variables.name: --dx-viz-purple
variables.paints: the sixth series colour

variables.name: --dx-viz-primary
variables.paints: the range selector: the selected range, the slider handle and its marker. The one place a chart follows --dx-accent-color, because the range selector is an editor and its selection is the accented control of the page it sits on

variables.name: --dx-viz-tooltip-bg
variables.paints: the tooltip plate and the annotation plate, inverted against the page so they read as something laid over it

variables.name: --dx-viz-tooltip-content
variables.paints: the text on those plates

variables.name: --dx-viz-font-family
variables.paints: every text the widget draws, titles included. It reads the page's own font name, so a chart is typeset like the widgets around it, and it is declared on the mode scopes because the name it reads is
